title: Universal Transformers
relevance_reason: Founding weight-tied depth-recurrent Transformer with per-position ACT halting; ancestor of all LoopLMs.
one_sentence: Introduces the Universal Transformer: one self-attention plus transition block, tied across depth, applied T times (encoder and decoder), with sinusoidal position+timestep embeddings and optional per-position ACT halting; beats Transformers on bAbI, LAMBADA, algorithmic tasks and WMT14.
key_contributions: Recurrence over depth (not positions) with weights tied across all steps; fixed-T UT equals a tied multi-layer Transformer
Per-position dynamic halting via ACT, with a 2D (position, time-step) coordinate embedding added at every step

title: Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA
relevance_reason: Converts pretrained LLMs into looped (CYCLE-tied) models and relaxes tying with per-iteration LoRA; defines the LoRA-relaxed sharing axis.
one_sentence: Initializes a looped block from a pretrained LLM (Stepwise/Average/Lower), uptrains on up to 60B tokens with distillation, adds per-loop LoRA deltas (SVD-initialized) to interpolate between tied and full models, and proposes continuous depth-wise batching with early exit.
key_contributions: Recursive Transformer: CYCLE tying of a block of L/B layers looped B times, initialized from a pretrained dense model (Stepwise best for strict tying, Average best with LoRA)
Relaxed Recursive Transformer: iteration-specific LoRA modules on all shared linear weights, initialized by truncated SVD of residuals; rank interpolates between recursive and vanilla
Continuous depth-wise batching + early exit; simulated throughput gains up to 2.66x

title: PonderLM: Pretraining Language Models to Ponder in Continuous Space
relevance_reason: Re-invokes the whole LM s times per token, feeding back a probability-weighted embedding; a whole-stack loop with a vocabulary-space bottleneck, pretrained at up to 2.8B/300B.
one_sentence: PonderLM runs the full LM repeatedly within one token step, turning each predicted distribution into a top-K weighted embedding that is residually added to the original input embeddings; PonderPythia trained on 300B Pile tokens beats official Pythia at equal parameters and data.
key_contributions: Pondering loop: state passed between iterations is the expected token embedding under the model's own prediction (top-K=100), accumulated onto the original input embeddings
Pretraining from scratch on GPT-2, LLaMA and Pythia architectures (405M-1.4B and Pythia suite to 2.8B on the full 300B-token Pile)
Ablation at 70M against hidden-state feedback, projected hidden state, looped Transformer and pause tokens at equal extra steps; randomized steps [1,10] yields test-time scaling

title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning
relevance_reason: Shares one global FFN 'Memory' (MoE-partitioned) across all layers with per-layer attention Reasoners and describes latent recurrence, but the text never specifies a loop count, iteration rule or tied block; component-level cross-depth sharing.
one_sentence: Mobius decouples knowledge (a single globally shared, MoE-partitioned FFN memory) from reasoning (attention Reasoners) so every layer can query all knowledge; a 7B-A1B model from scratch matches a Transformer with 62.6% of the data, and a Qwen3.5-35B conversion gives ~4x end-to-end speedup via shorter CoT.
key_contributions: Global shared FFN knowledge pool (horizontal concatenation of FFNs, block-wise MoE partition at scale) accessed by all attention layers: 'backward residual connection'
Training-from-scratch 7B-A1B comparison vs Transformer on 1TB tokens; continual pretraining of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 1TB tokens plus SFT and RL
Claims of dynamic latent reasoning and multi-token (MTP) drafting, with shorter CoT driving end-to-end throughput

The 7B-A1B from-scratch run is the only controlled comparison (iso-param, same data). Treat loop-related claims ('dynamic latent reasoning') as unquantified.

title: Recursive Inference Scaling: A Winning Path to Scalable Inference in Language and Multimodal Systems
relevance_reason: Compute-matched comparison of 59 parameter-sharing/recursion signatures; finds recursing the first half of the network (A^r B) best.
one_sentence: Under matched parameters and training FLOPs, RINS (split the model into equal halves A,B and apply A r times before B) beats 55+ sharing variants including MobileLLM's repeat-all-over and Huginn-style AB^rC, improves scaling exponents, and with stochastic depth plus linear adapters is no-regret.
key_contributions: Signature/degree taxonomy of recursive architectures and a training-FLOP-matched sweep (59 models, 300M/600M) where recursive models see fewer tokens
RINS (A^r B) wins; optimal r grows with training compute; fitted data scaling laws show better exponent and asymptote
Stochastic RINS (binomial number of rounds) with per-r linear output adapters (<1% params) is no-regret at 1x inference; KV-cache sharing variant; gains in SigLIP but not in supervised ViT

title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
relevance_reason: Probabilistic halting for any recurrent step function (incl. UT-style transformers); the standard learned-exit objective reused by later LoopLMs.
one_sentence: PonderNet makes halting a Markov process with per-step conditional halting probabilities, trains on the expected loss over all steps plus a KL to a geometric prior, and samples the halt at test time; it beats ACT on parity extrapolation and uses fewer steps than UT on bAbI.
key_contributions: Halting as a generalized geometric distribution over steps, with exact, unbiased, low-variance gradients (vs ACT and REINFORCE)
Loss = expected per-step reconstruction loss + KL(p_n || truncated geometric prior lambda_p) that encourages exploration rather than minimal steps
Train/test asymmetry: unroll until cumulative halting probability exceeds 1 - epsilon in training, sample Bernoulli halts at evaluation

setup.train_tokens_or_data: parity (64-element vectors; extrapolation trained on 1-48, tested on 49-96 ones), bAbI joint 10k, paired associative inference
setup.loops_train: unrolled until cumulative halting probability > 1 - epsilon (epsilon = 0.05), expected loss over steps
setup.loops_test: sampled halting per step, optionally capped at N

setup.benchmarks: parity interpolation/extrapolation, bAbI 20 tasks, PAI

title: Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks
relevance_reason: Weight-tied recurrent residual block between an encoder and head, trained on easy problems and unrolled longer at test; foundational easy-to-hard loop extrapolation evidence (vision/algorithmic, not language).
one_sentence: Recurrent ResNets (encoder, 4-layer weight-tied block iterated, conv head) trained on small prefix-sum, maze and chess instances solve larger/harder instances by running more iterations at test time, outperforming feed-forward nets of equal effective depth.
key_contributions: Easy-to-hard 'logical extrapolation' protocol with datasets of quantifiable difficulty (prefix sums, mazes, chess puzzles)
Recurrent vs feed-forward models matched on effective depth (only difference: weight sharing) show recurrent models extrapolate better
Test-time extra iterations improve accuracy on harder problems; per-iteration outputs resemble sequential algorithms; confidence used to pick the output iteration

title: MoRE: Mixture of Reused Experts
relevance_reason: Cross-layer sharing of MoE expert pools between adjacent layers with per-layer routers and depth embeddings; not iterating a block, but a sharing-axis design between MoE and MoEUT.
one_sentence: MoRE ties expert pools across groups of R adjacent layers (A-A-B-B), keeping per-layer routers and attention and adding a learnable depth embedding before routing; it beats DeepSeek-v3-style MoE, dense and MoEUT at matched parameters and FLOPs from 114M to 1.15B.
key_contributions: Reuse blocks: R adjacent layers share a 2N expert pool, enlarging routing combinations without extra parameters and allowing the same expert at consecutive depths
Learnable per-layer depth embedding added before routing so shared experts know their depth
Matched-parameter, matched-FLOP and matched-expert comparisons with paired bootstrap significance; block (consecutive) sharing beats non-aligned and random sharing

claims.evidence_quote: MoRE consistently achieves lower perplexity and stronger downstream performance than standard MoEs and state-of-the-art weight-sharing architectures at matched compute and parameter budgets

claims.evidence_quote: Block sharing achieves the lowest PPL (18.71), outperforming both Non-aligned (18.82) and Random sharing (18.83), the latter of which averages around the performance of the DeepSeek baseline.

Agrees with ALBERT/RINS that what is shared and where matters (block > random). Depth embedding here is a step-conditioning signal, cf. timestep debates (Huginn vs 2609.36636).

title: CART: Context-Anchored Recurrent Transformer -- A Parameter-Efficient Architecture with Learned Stability
relevance_reason: Prelude/shared-core/coda looped LM where the core cross-attends to a KV anchor computed once by the prelude, with an LTI stability gate; reports careful negative results.
one_sentence: CART computes K,V once from a P-layer prelude (MLA) and has a shared core cross-attend to that frozen anchor for R loops with a sigmoid LTI gate; at ~1B tokens it loses to parameter-matched dense baselines and extra test-time loops hurt.
key_contributions: Once-computed KV anchor: shared-weight core cross-attends causally to prelude K,V rather than re-injecting the prelude state additively or by concatenation
Sigmoid-gated LTI residual h <- sigma(a)*h_in + f(h) guaranteeing spectral radius < 1; learned rho settles in [0.79, 0.83]

Two-stage single-GPU study (64 configs at ~49M tokens, 36 configs at ~1B tokens) showing short-run hyperparameter rankings reverse, prelude depth beats loop count, and loops lose to dense at parameter parity

claims.evidence_quote: running more iterations than trained consistently degrades performance on HellaSwag, LAMBADA, and PIQA, a clean negative result for test-time compute scaling under our recipe.

claims.evidence_quote: The hyperparameter ordering P =6 > P =4 > P =3 > P =2 holds without exception across all R values and all four scales.

Novel injection operator: cross-attention to a once-computed KV anchor instead of additive/concat injection (design-space entry under KV sharing). Agrees with 2609.36636 and RINS that unshared prelude depth matters. Methodological warning: short screens mis-rank loop counts.

title: Ouroboros: Dynamic Weight Generation for Recursive Transformers via Input-Conditioned LoRA
relevance_reason: Retrofits a pretrained LLM into prelude / one looped layer / coda with a hypernetwork that generates per-step, input-conditioned LoRA modulation and a gated recurrence.
one_sentence: Ouroboros keeps 17 of Qwen2.5-3B's 36 layers (8 prelude, 1 looped layer, 8 coda, all frozen), loops the middle layer N times with a Controller that outputs per-step diagonal modulations of frozen SVD-initialized LoRA bases, plus an identity-biased gate; training loss improves but held-out loss does not.
key_contributions: Controller hypernetwork (mean-pooled hidden state + step embedding) producing input-dependent diagonal modulation of 7 LoRA targets per recurrence step
Frozen LoRA bases initialized by SVD of removed layers' weight residuals; gated recurrence biased to 88% retention plus per-step LayerNorm
Ablation vs static per-step LoRA over depths 1-16 and ranks 8-64; honest report of no held-out improvement

setup.model_sizes: Qwen2.5-3B pruned to 17 layers; 9.2M trainable parameters
setup.train_tokens_or_data: FineWeb-edu (token count not stated)

claims.evidence_quote: yet outperforms equivalently-sized static per-step LoRA by 1.44 loss points at depth 1 and remains ahead across all tested depths (1, 4, 8, 16) and ranks (8, 32, 64).

claims.evidence_quote: We also find that gated recurrence is essential: without it, recursive layer application makes the model strictly worse.

survey_notes: Represents 'dynamic generated weights' on the sharing axis (input-conditioned per-step LoRA via hypernetwork), beyond static per-step LoRA (Relaxed Recursive, RingFormer). Weak evidence: training-loss only, no held-out gains, so treat as a design proposal. Supports gating as necessary for deep recursion (cf. CART's LTI gate 2606.01495). The PDF carries a NeurIPS 2023 template footer, so venue is left null.

title: Looped Transformers with Source-Centered State Evolution
relevance_reason: Proposes a new state-passing/injection rule for looped Transformers: evolve deviations from a once-computed input anchor with a zero-deviation mask, instead of additive source re-injection.
one_sentence: SCSE computes an input-conditioned anchor h* once, recurs only on the deviation from it with a mask making the anchor an exact fixed point (removing the 'zero-deviation forcing bias' of additive injection), and lowers perplexity across loop depths versus additive-injection, tuned and step-conditioned shared-block baselines up to 139.2M parameters.
key_contributions: Identifies a source-driven degree of freedom (zero-deviation forcing bias) created by additive input re-injection in looped Transformers
Source-centered recurrence in anchor coordinates with a zero-deviation mask: exact anchor invariance by construction while nonzero deviations drive computation
Controlled comparisons against looped, tuned-adapter, capacity-matched and sinusoidal step-conditioned baselines; training with loop depth sampled uniformly in 1-8, evaluation to T=48

setup.train_tokens_or_data: WikiText-2, WikiText-103, direct web-corpus pretraining (token counts not stated in extracted text)
setup.loops_test: fixed T in {4,8,12,16,24,32,48} and adaptive stopping
setup.baselines: additive-injection looped Transformer, tuned adapter, recurrent-step-conditioned adapter, parameter-matched unshared controls

claims.evidence_quote: The capacity-matched and tuned adapters are substantially stronger than the looped Transformer baseline, yet SCSE attains lower mean PPL than all three baselines at every loop depth reported in Appendix Table 5.

claims.claim: Sinusoidal recurrent-step conditioning is a strong baseline at 50M (151.1 to 125.7 PPL at T=8) but SCSE remains best at every depth (123.1 at T=8, 156.4 at T=48).
claims.evidence_quote: At this scale, SCSE attains the lowest PPL among the compared sharedblock methods at every measured loop depth, reaching 123.1 at T = 8, 135.5 at T = 24, and 156.4 at T = 48.

claims.claim: The theory shows the forcing bias of additive injection can be harmful, neutral or beneficial; SCSE fixes it to zero for exact anchor invariance.
claims.evidence_quote: Our theory shows that the zero-deviation forcing bias is a design degree of freedom whose task effect can be harmful, neutral, or beneficial

numbers.what: Step-conditioned adapter vs looped baseline at 50M (T=8, T=48)
numbers.quote: The adapter improves the looped Transformer baseline from 151.1 to 125.7 PPL at T = 8 and from 178.9 to 160.1 at T = 48.

context lengths from 128 to 1024, and shared-block comparisons up to 139.2M parameters, SCSE improves the controlled recurrent quality frontier.

title: Reshape and Recur: Improving SSMs with Input Reshaping and Depth Recurrence
relevance_reason: Depth recurrence (periodic weight tying, AAAAAA/ABABAB/ABCABC) applied to SSM stacks on time-series classification/regression; not language.
one_sentence: Loops SSM blocks across depth with periodic tying patterns (period m in {1,2,3,6} for L=6), optional block-wise supervision and a prediction-change stopping rule, matching independent 6-block SSMs with 5.3-5.9x fewer parameters on time-series tasks; input reshaping is a complementary gain.
key_contributions: Periodic depth-recurrence family AAAAAA/ABABAB/ABCABC/ABCDEF for four SSMs (LRU, S5, LinOSS, LrcSSM)
Final-layer vs block-wise loss supervision and an adaptive stopping rule on relative prediction change
Input reshaping (concatenate or re-chunk time steps) as an orthogonal improvement

key_contributions: Universal expert pool reused across layers (virtual width) under fixed activated parameters
Staggered rotational connectivity, depth-aware exposure-corrected load balancing, and a dual-pathway router with an online fast-weight state over depth
Progressive conversion of existing MoE checkpoints into MoUE

relevance_reason: Represents each block's neurons as linear combinations of a shared set of neural bases (cross-layer basis reuse for compression); no block is iterated in depth and no loop count.
one_sentence: LRNBA builds attention and FFN blocks from coefficient-weighted combinations of shared reusable neural bases, enabling wider/deeper nets at a fixed parameter budget; on WikiText-2 an 8-layer variant reaches lower training loss with about 3/4 of the parameters but higher training time.
key_contributions: Neural-basis view of FFN blocks (sensor/response parameters) shared across blocks via coefficient tables
Extension to attention and projection blocks and sub-neural reuse
Small-scale function-fitting and WikiText-2 language-model experiments

title: Depth-Recurrent Attention Mixtures: Giving Latent Reasoning the Attention it Deserves
relevance_reason: Fully depth-recurrent single-layer MoE LM with attention along depth (to earlier depth states) and expert attention; FLOP-, parameter- and memory-matched against layered MoE.
one_sentence: Dreamer makes the whole model one depth-recurrent layer combining sequence attention, depth attention (attending over the token's previous depth states to relieve the fixed hidden-size bottleneck) and sparse expert attention (MoE), and needs 2-8x fewer training tokens than matched layered MoE on math reasoning.
key_contributions: Depth attention: attention along the depth dimension over earlier recurrent states (history injection), analogous to sequence attention fixing RNN bottlenecks
Fully depth-recurrent design (no fixed prelude/coda) with sparse expert attention, depth-position-encoded routing and RMSNorm applied to the residual stream
Tightly FLOP-, parameter- and memory-matched comparison with a layered SOTA-style MoE at depth 16 (~1B) and 32 (~2B) on ~100B tokens

setup.train_tokens_or_data: ca. 100B tokens of open instruction datasets with CoT traces removed; 25B-token ablations
setup.baselines: LA (layered non-recurrent MoE), DR without depth attention
setup.benchmarks: validation perplexity, math reasoning benchmarks (e.g. GSM8K)

claims.claim: Naive weight reuse across depth breaks residual scale compatibility; normalizing the residual stream itself is needed, and forcing attention projections to be reused hurts unless re-parameterized.
claims.evidence_quote: However, when increasing the depth, the scales of residuals and their additive updates can become incompatible across depths, which prevents learning depth-generalized experts.

claims.evidence_quote: We further present insights into knowledge usage across depths, e.g., showing 2 to 11× larger expert selection diversity than SOTA MoEs.

numbers.quote: We compare three main architecture variants, at depth 16 (ca. 1B parameters) and depth 32 (ca. 2B parameters)

title: Mobius Learning: Cyclic Depth Folding in Transformers
relevance_reason: Looped Transformer variant where different data streams traverse the shared block groups in cyclically shifted orders, so each group serves shallow and deep roles.
one_sentence: Mobius Learning partitions a Transformer into P=4 block groups held by different workers and feeds each worker's data starting at its own group, so streams loop through cyclically shifted orders; at loop depths 6-15 on GPT-2 small it beats fixed-order looping at matched tokens and depth.
key_contributions: Cyclic depth folding: worker-indexed cyclic block orders make each block group act at every source-relative depth (depth-role superposition)
Matched comparison with ordered-loop training at the same loop depth L (K=4L block-group applications) and token budget
Distributed 'Mobius parallelism': each worker stores one block group and keeps raw data local

title: Share Your Attention: Transformer Weight Sharing via Matrix-based Dictionary Learning
relevance_reason: Cross-layer sharing of attention projections via shared matrix-atom dictionaries; compression, not iterated depth; compares to repeat-all-over and sequential sharing.
one_sentence: MASA represents each layer's Q/K/V/O matrices as linear combinations of a shared dictionary of matrix atoms, cutting attention parameters by 66.7% at on-par quality and beating GQA, low-rank, repeat-all-over and sequential sharing at matched parameter budgets (100M-700M).
key_contributions: Matrix-atom dictionary shared across layers for attention projections (layer-specific coefficients)
Drop-in replacement trained with standard optimizers; also applied to ViT and to pretrained LLMs
Comparisons with repeat-all-over (MobileLLM) and sequential sharing at comparable parameter budgets

setup.baselines: GQA, low-rank, Repeat-all-over, Sequential sharing
setup.benchmarks: perplexity and benchmark accuracy; ViT image classification

claims.claim: At comparable parameter budgets, dictionary-shared attention beats GQA, low-rank and repeat-all-over/sequential layer sharing.
claims.evidence_quote: Experiments across scales (100M–700M parameters) show that MASA achieves better benchmark accuracy and perplexity than grouped-query attention (GQA), low-rank baselines and recently proposed Repeat-all-over/Sequential sharing at comparable parameter budgets.

title: AbbIE: Autoregressive Block-Based Iterative Encoder for Efficient Sequence Modeling
relevance_reason: Head/Body/Tail looped decoder LM (Body iterated r times) comparing plain chaining vs an inter-iteration residual for input injection; trained with 2 iterations, extrapolates at test time.
one_sentence: AbbIE splits a Transformer into Head, iterated Body and Tail; the AbbIE-D variant adds an inter-iteration residual (input re-injection) that converges to a fixed point while plain chaining (AbbIE-C) diverges, and with only 2 training iterations it extrapolates to more test iterations, improving perplexity up to 5% and ICL up to 12% at <=350M.
key_contributions: Head (token->concept space) / Body (iterated) / Tail decomposition, trained with r=2 iterations
Two injection variants: AbbIE-C (chain outputs) vs AbbIE-D (inter-iteration residual, diffusion-inspired); only AbbIE-D reaches a fixed point
Upward generalization to more test-time iterations without specialized data

setup.train_tokens_or_data: compute-optimal budget of 20 tokens per parameter and multiples; sequence length 2048
setup.baselines: standard Transformer (STD), Depth (path-independent recurrent baseline)
setup.benchmarks: perplexity, zero-shot ICL (HellaSwag, LAMBADA, ARC-Easy, CommonsenseQA)

claims.claim: Plain chaining of iterations (AbbIE-C) fails to converge; an extra inter-iteration residual (AbbIE-D) reaches a fixed point like the path-independent Depth baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: In contrast, AbbIE-C fails to converge after 32 iterations. This shows that the residual steam, present in the body of Transformer, is in itself not sufficient and an extra inter-iteration residual connection is needed.

claims.claim: At the same size and token budget, AbbIE beats the standard Transformer and Depth baseline in perplexity, but at a higher FLOP cost.
claims.evidence_quote: Across all configurations, AbbIE consistently outperforms both the standard Transformer and Depth baseline in terms of perplexity.

claims.claim: Training with only 2 iterations suffices for upward generalization, giving up to 12% ICL and 5% perplexity improvements when scaling test-time iterations.
claims.evidence_quote: We show that AbbIE upward generalizes (ability to generalize to arbitrary iteration lengths) at test time by only using 2 iterations during train time, far outperforming alternative iterative methods.

numbers.value: up to 12% zero-shot ICL, up to 5% perplexity
numbers.quote: gives it an up to 12% improvement in zero-shot in-context learning tasks versus other iterative and standard methods and up to 5% improvement in language perplexity.
We perform all of our evaluations on model sizes up to 350M parameters.

limitations: Up to 350M; higher training FLOPs than standard Transformer (authors hypothesize convergence for very long runs); AbbIE-C discarded.
survey_notes: Injection-type evidence: an explicit inter-iteration residual (input injection) is required for convergence/extrapolation; supports Huginn-style injection and contrasts with 2609.36636 which finds lightweight initial-state injection gives negligible gains over no injection (but there the dense variant collapses). Training with only 2 loops and extrapolating is a cheap regime; compute-matching is absent (iso-param/iso-data only).

title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
relevance_reason: Self-iterates a (single-layer/few-layer) SSM or transformer block to an approximate fixed point (DEQ-style, phantom gradients) and pretrains up to 1.3B on 207B tokens.
one_sentence: Implicit SSMs/transformers iterate a block with additive input injection until (approximate) fixed-point convergence, which theoretically yields RNN-like non-linear state transitions; a bounded-iteration curriculum with phantom gradients scales them to 1.3B/207B tokens, where they beat explicit counterparts and solve state tracking.
key_contributions: Theory: implicit (fixed-point) SSMs implement non-linear, non-diagonal state transitions like RNNs, solving the S5 word problem
Approximate convergence suffices: curriculum bounding iterations retains parallelism; phantom-gradient (truncated implicit) backprop
Largest self-iterated models with dynamic halting to date (implicit Mamba2 and Llama3 up to 1.3B on 207B D-Pile tokens), with length generalization and path independence

one_sentence: RingFormer applies a single shared Transformer layer repeatedly (encoder-decoder for MT, ViT for images) and adds per-depth low-rank transformations of the input that generate level signals for Q/K/V and FFN plus per-iteration LayerNorm, matching vanilla Transformers on WMT14 De-En and ImageNet with fewer parameters and beating Universal Transformers.
key_contributions: Input-dependent level signals from depth-specific low-rank matrices injected into attention projections and FFN of a shared block
Per-level unique layer normalization
Evaluation on WMT-14 De-En translation and ImageNet-small/1K against vanilla Transformer, One Wide FFN and Universal Transformer

title: Basis Sharing: Cross-Layer Parameter Sharing for Large Language Model Compression
relevance_reason: Post-training SVD compression sharing basis vectors across layers with layer-specific coefficients; no iterated depth.
one_sentence: Basis Sharing compresses pretrained LLMs by decomposing weight matrices of groups of layers into shared SVD bases plus unique per-layer coefficients, beating SVD-based compression by up to 25% perplexity reduction at 20-50% compression without fine-tuning.
key_contributions: Cross-layer shared SVD basis with layer-specific coefficients
Study of which weight types and layer groups can share bases
Training-free compression of LLaMA-family models at 20-50% ratios

setup.baselines: SVD-based compression (e.g. SVD-LLM), parameter sharing techniques
setup.benchmarks: perplexity on generation tasks, downstream reasoning accuracy

claims.claim: At the same compression ratio, cross-layer basis sharing reduces perplexity by up to 25% and improves downstream accuracy by up to 4% over SVD-based compression.
claims.evidence_quote: compared with state-ofthe-art SVD-based compression approaches, Basis Sharing can further reduce the perplexity by up to 25% on generation tasks and improve accuracy by up to 4% on downstream reasoning tasks under the same compression ratio.

limitations: Compression only; no extra depth or test-time compute.
survey_notes: Out of scope for looping; cite only as part of the cross-layer compression lineage (with MASA 2508.04581, LRNBA 2609.01550). Its premise that brute-force tying hurts because layers should differ echoes Relaxed Recursive Transformers' motivation for LoRA relaxation.

title: On the Design Space Between Transformers and Recursive Neural Nets
relevance_reason: Analysis/position paper connecting UT-style shared-layer Transformers (Neural Data Router) and continuous recursive neural nets; algorithmic tasks.
one_sentence: Formalizes the connection between Continuous Recursive Neural Networks and Neural Data Routers (a gated, geometric-attention UT variant), arguing tasks like ListOps need arbitrary-order composition, gating and adaptive depth, and evaluating both on length/depth generalization.
key_contributions: Requirements C1-C3 (arbitrary-order composition, gating, adaptive depth) for structured reasoning tasks
Shows CRvNN and NDR converge toward a shared design between RvNNs and Transformers
Identifies NDR's lack of dynamic halting (max depth set a priori) as a key limitation

Analysis of sharing group size K: sharing across 3 layers costs 4% relative WER, larger groups cost more
Comparison with smaller non-shared encoders of equal size

Released compact pretrained models

survey_notes: Key controlled evidence for the 'design space' section: it matches physical depth, training effective depth, inference effective depth and data. Agrees with prelude/coda (sandwich) designs but adds nuance: coda for under-unrolling robustness, prelude for extrapolation. The reasoning-up/knowledge-down split under extra loops is a central caveat for 'loops as test-time compute'. Also: Huginn-style 1+2x5+1 failed to train with AdamW (optimizer sensitivity).

title: CoTFormer: A Chain-of-Thought Driven Architecture with Budget-Adaptive Computation Cost at Inference
relevance_reason: Weight-tied repeated block where each repeat's outputs are appended as new tokens that later repeats attend to; token-level adaptive repeats with budget control.
one_sentence: CoTFormer argues CoT differs from weight-tied depth because thought tokens attend to earlier intermediate states; it interleaves each repeat's representations into the attention context, beats Block Universal Transformers at equal size and repeats, and adds MoD-style per-repeat routing for inference-time budget control.
key_contributions: Distinguishes Block Universal Transformers (tied N-layer block repeated) from CoT: in CoTFormer later repeats attend to all tokens' representations from all previous repeats
LN-CoTFormer: reserved unshared beginning/final layers (2 -> 21x5 -> 1), layer norm after each repeat; 24x5 beats a 48-layer standard Transformer
Mixture-of-Repeats adaptive training: per-repeat routers with randomly sampled capacities, interpolation x(i+1)=(1-s)x(i)+s B(x(i)), and a depth embedding, enabling inference-time compute budgets

setup.model_sizes: 12- and 24-layer bases (hidden 768, 12 heads) repeated 2-5 times; standard 12/24/48-layer baselines (parameter counts not stated)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: OpenWebText2; 40k steps (60k for adaptive), batch 128 sequences of length 256
setup.loops_train: fixed nrepeat in {2,3,5}; adaptive model samples random per-repeat capacities with max 5 repeats
setup.loops_test: fixed repeats, or router-based capacity / threshold chosen at inference to set compute budget
setup.baselines: Block Universal Transformer (same layers and repeats), adaptive Block UT with Mixture of Repeats, standard 12/24/48-layer Transformers
setup.benchmarks: OpenWebText2 perplexity; MACs vs perplexity Pareto

claims.claim: At equal parameters and equal number of repeats, CoTFormer beats Block Universal Transformer in perplexity, and the gap widens with more repeats (at the cost of extra attention compute).
claims.evidence_quote: It can be clearly seen that CoTFormers significantly outperform Block Universal Transformers with the same size and the same number of repeated applications of the model.

claims.claim: At matched MACs, CoTFormer sits on the perplexity-compute Pareto front: a 12x3 CoTFormer is cheaper than a 12x5 Block UT of similar accuracy even at sequence length 8192.
claims.evidence_quote: It can be seen that even for sequences as long as 8192, the 12x3 CoTFormer's cost remains below that of 12x5 Block Universal Transformer.

claims.claim: With reserved unshared first/last layers and a layer norm after each repeat, a 24-layer CoTFormer with 5 repeats beats a standard 48-layer Transformer (24.11 vs 24.17 ppl); but matching deeper models needs more repeats than the depth ratio.
claims.regime: unmatched depth (24x5 vs 48x1; half the unique layers, more compute)
claims.evidence_quote: Most noticeably, after applying these changes, the performance of a CoTFormer with 24 layers and 5 repeats, surpasses the performance of a standard 48 layer Transformer.

claims.claim: Router-based token allocation gives a much better compute-accuracy trade-off than uniformly truncating repeats at inference; but adaptive training lags a fixed-5-repeat model at equal inference compute (23.83 vs 23.19).
claims.evidence_quote: For example, after 60k steps, the former reaches perplexity 23.83 while the latter achieves 23.19.

claims.claim: A depth embedding conditioning on remaining repeats is neutral at fixed repeats but helps in the adaptive case.
claims.evidence_quote: While the performance is similar on fixed number of repeats, a noticeable boost is observed in the adaptive case.

claims.claim: Alternative adaptive-training methods for Universal Transformers (ACT/PonderNet-style) did not outperform at small scale, so a Mixture-of-Repeats adaptive Block UT is used as baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: While alternative methods for adaptive training of Universal Transformers have been proposed in the literature, we could not obtain a better performance using those methods in small scale experiments.

limitations: Small scale (OpenWebText2, 40-60k steps, seq length 256); attention cost grows with repeats; adaptive model underperforms fixed-depth at same compute; at zero repeats adaptive Block UT beats adaptive CoTFormer; needs more repeats than the depth ratio to match deeper dense models; LN-CoTFormer shows loss spikes.
survey_notes: Lineage: introduces cross-iteration attention (history injection through the KV context), a precursor to KV/trajectory-sharing designs, and an early prelude-core-coda variant (2 -> 21x5 -> 1) with LN after each repeat and a remaining-depth embedding. Contrasts with Huginn-style models that avoid step conditioning (depth embedding here helps only for adaptive routing). Comparison regimes: Table 1 is iso-param and iso-repeats (but not iso-FLOP: CoTFormer pays extra attention); the 48-layer win is at 5x repeats, i.e. more compute. Reports that matching a 2x deeper dense model needs 5 repeats: evidence that loops are less efficient than unique layers per FLOP.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
relevance_reason: Shared-layer (UT) language model made parameter-competitive by MoE FFN and MoE attention inside the loop, with layer grouping and peri-layernorm.
one_sentence: MoEUT fixes the UT parameter-compute ratio by making the shared block a group of G=2-4 MoE layers (sigma-MoE FFN + SwitchHead attention) repeated 8-9 times with peri-layernorm, slightly beating parameter-matched dense Transformers up to 1B parameters at fewer MACs.
key_contributions: MoE FFN and MoE attention inside a shared layer to decouple parameters from compute in UTs
Layer grouping (ABAB stacking of G non-shared layers, G=2 best) and peri-layernorm (no layernorm on the residual/main data path) for shared-layer signal propagation
First UT to match or beat parameter-matched dense Transformers on LM (C4, SlimPajama, peS2o, The Stack), plus expert-reuse analysis across depth

setup.train_tokens_or_data: C4, SlimPajama, peS2o, The Stack subset; batch size 64, context length 1024, 10^5 steps for all models
setup.loops_train: fixed: group of G layers (2-4) repeated, typically 8 or 9 recurrent steps
setup.baselines: parameter-matched pre-LN dense Transformer, non-shared sigma-MoE, Sparse Universal Transformer (SUT)
setup.benchmarks: perplexity on C4/SlimPajama/peS2o/The Stack; zero-shot LAMBADA, BLiMP, CBT, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-E

claims.claim: MoEUT slightly outperforms dense Transformers with the same parameter count (same d_model and number of layers, same training steps), and the gap grows with scale, while using fewer MACs.
claims.evidence_quote: slightly outperforms dense models with the same number of parameters (Fig. 4a), and the gap tends to grow with scale.

claims.claim: At equal total training MACs, MoEUT beats the dense baseline by a large margin.
claims.evidence_quote: Given equal amounts of compute, MoEUT outperforms other models by a large margin.

claims.claim: Group size G=2 is optimal at 244M parameter-matched: both a single shared layer (G=1) and no sharing (G=18) are worse, and ABAB stacking beats AABB.
claims.evidence_quote: In Fig. 6, we observe that G = 2 is optimal, and the recurrence in the layer dimension is indeed beneficial.

claims.claim: ACT halting is the main cause of SUT's poor LM performance; removing ACT improves it dramatically, though it still trails MoEUT and dense baselines.
claims.evidence_quote: we found that most of this poor performance comes from the ACT mechanism that the authors advertise as one of the main components of their model.

claims.claim: Peri-layernorm is best, but its advantage over post-layernorm diminishes at larger scale.
claims.evidence_quote: the gap between peri-norm and post-norm is marginal: 11.29 perplexity points compared to 11.32).

claims.claim: Contrary to Takase & Kiyono's large groups with few steps, smaller groups with more recurrent steps perform better.
claims.evidence_quote: However, they consider models with large group sizes (G = 6 for 12 layers) and few recurrent steps (2). We find that models with smaller G with more steps perform better.

numbers.quote: All models are trained with batch size 64 and context length 1024, for 105 steps.
In our experiments, the group size is between 2 and 4, and the typical number of recurrent steps is 8 or 9.

numbers.quote: Compared to the standard Transformer with FlashAttention [56], our MoEUT model trains 1.5–2x slower.
outperforming standard Transformers with less compute and memory requirements on all scales on which we can afford to test (up to 1B parameters).

limitations: Modest training regime (10^5 steps, batch 64); suboptimal Triton MoE kernels make training 1.5-2x slower than dense; zero-shot differences vs baseline are marginal; no ACT studied.
venue: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024).
survey_notes: Key design-space entry for 'MoE-in-loop' sharing and for normalization as part of state carrying (peri-LN avoids residual norm growth across loop steps). Disagrees with Takase & Kiyono on grouping: small G with many steps beats large G with 2 steps. Contradicts ACT-based UTs (SUT) at LM scale: ACT hurt. Agrees with ALBERT that naive sharing is parameter-starved; resolves it with MoE. Regime is clean (parameter-matched, same steps), but only up to 1B and modest token budget.

title: LT2: Linear-Time Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Looped Transformers whose shared block uses linear/sparse/hybrid attention; studies interaction of the token mixer with looping and converts Ouro into a hybrid looped model.
one_sentence: LT2 replaces softmax attention in looped Transformers with linear (GDN, KDA), sparse (DSA, window) or hybrid mixers; looping refines linear-attention memory and expands sparse receptive fields, hybrids match or beat the full-attention loop at 5x decode throughput, and Ouro-1.4B converts with ~1B tokens.
key_contributions: Looped linear and sparse attention with theory: loops iteratively refine linear-attention memory; T loops of a window-w block reach as far as T stacked window layers
LT2-hybrid (GDN+DSA) matches the full-attention looped model without quadratic attention; (Full+GDN) at 1:4 ratio surpasses it
Distillation of Ouro into Ouro-hybrid-1.4B with ~1B tokens; SDPA output gate mitigates attention-sink amplification across loops

setup.train_tokens_or_data: FineWeb-Edu 100B tokens (from scratch); ~1B tokens continued training for conversion
setup.baselines: standard full-attention Looped Transformer; Ouro-1.4B teacher; industry 1B-4B models
setup.benchmarks: zero-shot downstream average, perplexity, synthetic recall and state tracking, prefill/decode throughput to 32k

claims.claim: At matched parameters, loops and data, LT2-hybrid (GDN+DSA) matches the full-attention looped Transformer's quality with ~5.7x higher decode throughput at 8k context; (Full+GDN) improves zero-shot by +2.1 points with ~5x throughput.
claims.evidence_quote: it improves average zero-shot performance by +2.1 points over the standard looped transformer (61.4% vs. 59.3%) while still achieving ∼5× higher decode throughput at the same setting

claims.claim: Looped GDN slightly trails the full-attention loop at 0.6B but surpasses it at 1.3B while keeping linear time.
claims.evidence_quote: At the smaller 0.6B scale, looped GDN still slightly trails the Looped Transformer; however, at the larger 1.3B scale, it surpasses the Looped Transformer while preserving linear-time complexity.

claims.claim: A pretrained looped model (Ouro) can be converted to a linear-time hybrid with ~1B tokens, retaining teacher quality; comparison to industry models is unmatched.
claims.evidence_quote: with only ∼1B tokens of continued training, our converted Ouro-Hybrid1.4B retains the quality of its full-attention teacher while inheriting LT2's linear-time efficiency.

claims.claim: Full-attention looped Transformers lose more than half of decode throughput from 4k to 32k because the KV cache grows per loop iteration; linear-time mixers keep a flat decode rate.
claims.evidence_quote: Looped Transformer loses more than half of its decode throughput between 4k and 32k because its KV cache keeps growing per loop iteration.

numbers.value: 0.6B and 1.3B, 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens, T=4 loops, 1:4 hybrid ratio
numbers.quote: We pre-train all models on FineWeb-Edu [46] at 0.6B and 1.3B parameters with a 100B-token budget, using T=4 loops for every looped variant.

numbers.what: Decode throughput at 8k context (GDN+DSA vs full-attention loop)
numbers.quote: delivering ∼5.7× higher decode throughput at 8k context (125 vs. 22 tokens/s, batch size 8), entirely without quadratic attention.

numbers.quote: Looped Hybrid (GDN+DSA), which contains no full attention, matches the full-attention reference at both scales (9.72 vs. 9.87 PPL at 1.3B).

limitations: Fixed 4 loops; up to 1.3B from scratch; pure DeltaNet loops unstable; conversion compared against public industry models (unmatched).
survey_notes: Hybrid design-space entry (looping x token mixer): looped linear attention behaves like iterative memory refinement; KV cache of full-attention loops grows per loop iteration, which LT2 avoids (systems relevance). Reports that weight-shared loops mildly amplify attention sinks and that an output gate mitigates it. Released weights (Ouro-hybrid-1.4B).

title: Looped Transformers as Optimizers
relevance_reason: Frames loop transitions (state injection/update rules) as optimizer steps on a fast-weight state and derives a new transition; middle-loop MoE LMs at 5B/10B total parameters.
one_sentence: Treats the looped hidden state as a fast weight updated by local gradient steps, derives loop transitions from a projection, objective and optimizer, aligns Parcae/HyperLoop read-write maps, and proposes OperLoop (weight decay, adaptive step size, delta objective), beating looped and non-looped baselines at matched training FLOPs.
key_contributions: Optimization view: a loop transition = closed-form local optimizer update with read/write projections; reveals input-map mismatches in Parcae and HyperLoop
Input-map alignment (transpose read/write) improves existing transitions with fewer parameters
OperLoop transition (explicit weight decay, adaptive causal step size, delta objective) on middle-loop MoE LMs with 4 parallel streams

setup.model_sizes: non-looped baselines 5B total / 600M active (18 layers) and 10B / 900M active (32 layers); looped variants ~50% of parameters
setup.train_tokens_or_data: ~300B tokens (5B scale) and ~500B tokens (10B scale), sequence length 4096
setup.baselines: non-looped MoE baselines, Parcae, HyperLoop, aligned variants
setup.benchmarks: commonsense LL accuracy, Wikitext/Lambada PPL, math/code/reasoning generation (e.g. 8-shot CoT GSM8K)

claims.claim: At matched unrolled training FLOPs and effective depth with about half the parameters, OperLoop raises the generative EM average over the non-looped baseline by 1.69 and 1.04 points at the two scales.
claims.evidence_quote: Relative to the non-looped baselines in Table 3, OperLoop uses approximately half the parameters while improving the EM average by 1.69 and 1.04 percentage points at the two scales.

claims.claim: Input-map alignment, derived from the optimizer view, improves existing transitions (HyperLoop 58.93 to 59.47 commonsense average) with fewer transition parameters.
claims.evidence_quote: For example, HyperLoop improves average accuracy from 58.93 to 59.47 while using fewer transition parameters.

claims.evidence_quote: For OperLoop, the EM average rises from 25.58 to 31.90, with 8-shot CoT GSM8K improving from 17.13

claims.claim: Even with 6 loops OperLoop still trails the non-looped baseline on Wikitext PPL and LL accuracy (while surpassing it on Lambada PPL), whereas generative EM improves: the evaluation metric changes the conclusion.

claims.evidence_quote: still trails the non-looped baseline on Wikitext PPL and LL accuracy while surpassing it on Lambada PPL.

claims.claim: At matched compute (Loop3), OperLoop exceeds the non-looped baseline in EM average despite worse PPL and LL accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: OperLoop exceeds the non-looped baseline in EM average

numbers.what: Looped variant parameter share and matching
numbers.value: ~50% of parameters, matched unrolled training FLOPs
numbers.quote: each looped variant uses the middle-loop pattern and matches the unrolled training FLOPs of its non-looped baseline, with approximately 50% as many parameters.

survey_notes: Design-space: the injection operator I(s,e) as an optimizer update (state decay = weight decay, adaptive step size, delta rule). Provides one of the largest-scale iso-train-FLOP/iso-effective-depth comparisons (5B/10B MoE, 300-500B tokens) where looping with half the parameters beats the non-looped model on generation EM but not always on PPL: metric choice changes conclusions (cf. knowledge/reasoning split in 2609.36636). Builds directly on Hyperloop's middle-loop + parallel streams.
